beats.vo_text: On April 14th, 1912, the largest moving object ever built by human hands was sailing through the freezing dark of the North Atlantic.
beats.visual_intent: Cinematic dark ocean at night with foggy atmosphere, viewed from the deck of a massive Edwardian luxury steamship cutting through icy black water.

beats.vo_text: The RMS Titanic set sail from Southampton with over two thousand passengers on board, bound for New York.
beats.visual_intent: Historical archival footage and sepia-toned photographs of passengers waving farewell from the crowded decks of the Titanic at Southampton dock.

beats.vo_text: Engineers believed she could survive flooding in any four of her sixteen watertight compartments. The iceberg breached six.
beats.visual_intent: Technical cutaway diagram of the RMS Titanic highlighting the sixteen watertight compartments across the ship's length.

beats.vo_text: At 11:40 PM, a lookout in the crow's nest spotted it too late. The ship struck the iceberg along her starboard side.
beats.visual_intent: Dramatic dramatization inside a dark crow's nest at night, looking down over the bow toward a towering shadowy iceberg dead ahead.

beats.vo_text: The order went out across the decks, as the crew scrambled to load the lifeboats.
beats.visual_intent: Panicked passengers and crew members gathering on the sloping deck of an ocean liner at night under emergency red and white lighting.

beats.vo_text: Titanic wasn't alone. Her sister ship, the Britannic, was nearly identical in design — and met her own disaster years later, sunk by a mine in the Aegean Sea during World War One.
beats.visual_intent: Comparative side-by-side architectural blueprint drawings of the RMS Titanic and her sister ship HMHS Britannic.

beats.vo_text: The wreck wasn't discovered until 1985, resting over twelve thousand feet down, split into two pieces on the ocean floor.
beats.visual_intent: Deep-sea underwater submersible spotlight illuminating the ghostly, rusted bow of the Titanic resting upright on the pitch-black ocean floor.
